causal_confidence.statement: Arg1274Trp has variant-specific reduced chromatin occupancy and cytoplasmic localization in engineered HepG2 cells, supporting a hypomorphic effect. This strengthens the proposed gene association but does not itself establish the packet SOLVED/CAUSATIVE/PATHOGENIC clinical classification. UNKNOWN_ACTIONABILITY is consistent with no demonstrated clinical intervention.

evidence.locator: Figures4/S7; Results PDF9-11; Discussion PDF12; ACMG EVIDENCE CODES PDF46

limitations: No formal ACMG classification applied by authors; engineered hepatoma cells are not patient neurons.
Modeling predicts stabilization at a low-confidence residue (pLDDT34.87), so hypomorphism must not be restated as proven protein destabilization.

segregation.statement: Trio Autism/ID panel identifies de novo ZMYM3 variant; Sanger confirms proband while parents have high-quality NGS and did not require Sanger confirmation. FigS1 shows both parents negative.

evidence.locator: Methods table PDF42; case report PDF27; FigS1 PDF32

phase.statement: Source is a heterozygous de novo X-linked variant, not a hemizygous state. No compound-heterozygous phase question. No X-inactivation result is reported for Individual19.

evidence.locator: Table1 PDF6; Results PDF7; case report PDF26-27

limitations: X-inactivation results for Individuals18 and20 cannot be transferred to Individual19.

causal_confidence.statement: Paper proposes ZMYM3 association, but Individual19 has a de novo ZMYM3 VUS plus paternal SCN2A c.1421T>A VUS, considered a poor fit by authors. Tyr752Cys has modeling evidence, not a patient-variant cell assay. Packet SOLVED/CAUSATIVE/PATHOGENIC and named OMIM diagnosis are stronger than this source establishes; infantile developmental presentation is supported. UNKNOWN_ACTIONABILITY matches the absence of demonstrated therapy.

evidence.locator: Case report PDF26-27; Discussion PDF11-12; ACMG EVIDENCE CODES PDF46; modeling TableS2 row15

limitations: Authors explicitly did not apply ACMG codes and say most variants would remain VUSs.
No individual-level functional demonstration for Tyr752Cys; absence of formal ID assessment in this young child must be retained.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Packet misses cardiac abnormalities, epicanthal folds, short nose, soft skin, poor weight gain, balance impairment and family connective-tissue history; it miscodes a heterozygous female as hemizygous. Speech improved after therapy.

evidence.locator: Supplemental case report Individual 19, PDF26-27; Table1 PDF6; Fig2 PDF8
